CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the June 1 retaliatory tariff increase and the announced but still-unpopulated unreliable-entity list, and take the late-June G20 Osaka meeting with Trump as the next negotiating window. Do not populate the unreliable list, cut rare-earth exports, or add new tariff lines before that meeting; those moves would give Washington a pretext to proceed with the remaining ~$300B tariff package and deepen the Huawei cutoff. Do not concede statutory structural changes or large purchase commitments unless the United States first freezes the remaining-tariff process and opens a path on Huawei licensing.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. On 10 May the US raised List 3 from 10% to 25%, putting ~$250B of Chinese exports at 25%, and directed preparation of tariffs on the remaining ~$300B (timeline 2019-05-05, 2019-05-10). The 16 May Huawei Entity Listing plus Google/chip-supplier cutoffs on 20 May strike a national champion and export-tech ambitions: nearly half of Huawei smartphone shipments are outside China and future devices lose GMS/Android licensing (timeline 2019-05-15/16/20; CNBC/Verge 20 May). CNY weakened from ~6.73 in April to 6.91 by early June after the breakdown, matching the CHN +0.5 FX-pressure anchor (DEXCHUS / EXCHUS). That is not +1.0: industrial production is still +5.0 to +6.3% y/y, merchandise exports are roughly flat near $210B, and reserves rose to ~$3.14T (country_health). Talks collapsed because Beijing refused to write IP/tech-transfer/SOE commitments into statute after months of draft progress (NYT/CNBC 10–13 May; Liu He: principle issues; People's Daily: will not swallow 'bitter fruit'). Further Chinese escalation now has little tariff ammunition left (~$60B already re-rated) and would risk locking in the $300B list and a faster tech decoupling China is not ready for. A G20 meeting is already publicly expected (Trump/Kudlow mid-May) and no working-level round is scheduled, so the disciplined stance is negotiate without new commitments: keep existing counters as leverage, leave rare earths and the unreliable list as unused options, and test whether Washington will trade a tariff freeze and licensing flexibility for limited, non-statutory implementation language.
key_factors: List 3 now at 25% on ~$200B; remaining ~$300B tariff package prepared but not yet imposed
Huawei Entity List plus Google/Qualcomm/Intel supply cut — firm-level tech shock, not just tariffs
Talks stalled on writing structural IP/tech-transfer commitments into Chinese law
CNY weakened toward 6.91 after May breakdown, but reserves rose and IP/exports have not cracked
China already raised tariffs on ~$60B US goods (1 June) and announced an unreliable-entity list — further tariff room is thin
G20 Osaka (28–29 June) is the next presidential off-ramp; no interim working-level talks scheduled

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump tweets negotiations going too slowly and China attempting to renegotiate; orders List 3 raised from 10% to 25% on May 10 and directs preparation of tariffs on remaining Chinese imports (~$300B).
List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
Google suspends Huawei's access to Android updates / GMS; major US chip suppliers pause sales. Same day: Xi Jinping visits a rare-earth facility in Jiangxi.
China announces it will raise retaliatory tariff rates on its ~$60B US-goods list (higher rates phased in; many effective June 1).
China announces it will establish an unreliable entity list targeting foreign firms that cut supplies to Chinese companies for non-commercial reasons.
CNY/USD weakened from ~6.73 in late April to 6.9084 on 2019-06-05 after the May breakdown.
China total reserves excluding gold rose to ~$3.14T as of 2019-06-01 — no reserve-drain crisis.
China industrial production still expanding: 105.0 in May and 106.3 in June (index, same period previous year = 100).
Google suspends hardware/software/technical services to Huawei; future phones lose licensed Android/GMS. ~49% of Q1 2019 Huawei smartphone shipments were outside mainland China.
People's Daily: China will not swallow bitter fruit that harms core interests. US insists structural changes be written into Chinese law, not merely State Council decrees.
Trump says he will meet Xi at the G20 in Osaka June 28–29; he has not yet decided whether to proceed with tariffs on the remaining ~$325B.
